note: Third full-tier run. The brief is BYTE-IDENTICAL to run 2's tree (git diff a2c77e5..6e4d537 -- .abcd/development/brief/ is empty), so run 2 vs run 3 is a controlled stability measurement with the detector's own subject held constant.

discrepancies.claim: "The `/abcd:ahoy` slash command dispatches every sub-verb (`status | install | uninstall | doctor | dry-run`) … and each also ships on the CLI as `abcd ahoy <sub-verb>`."
discrepancies.reality: `./bin/abcd-darwin-arm64 ahoy status` → `abcd: unknown command "status" for "abcd ahoy"`. `abcd ahoy --help` lists exactly doctor, dry-run, identity-check, install, uninstall — `status` is a slash-command-only alias for the bare pass (commands/ahoy.md: "No argument, or `status`, is the bare read-only detection pass"), and it does not ship on the CLI.

discrepancies.claim: The PATH entry is a symlink: detection "scan[s] `PATH` for `abcd`, resolving symlinks" and asks "Install `abcd` symlink to `~/.local/bin/abcd`?", writing it when "the target is absent or already points at this plugin".
discrepancies.reality: internal/core/ahoy/owned_copy.go:13-22 — the shipped entry is an abcd-owned regular-file COPY of the verified release artefact from the plugin data dir's cache (spc-35), because "a symlink into the plugin root dies at every plugin update"; ownership is RECORDED PROVENANCE in `~/.abcd/path-entry` (installed path + SHA-256), not "points at this plugin". The pinned symlink survives only as a loud degradation when no verified cache artefact exists (owned_copy.go:186-199). The CLI confirms the model: `abcd ahoy uninstall --help` → "Remove the marker block, abcd's owned PATH copy, and its provenance record".

discrepancies.claim: Uninstall "removes the marker block and abcd's own `PATH` entry (if owned by this plugin)" and "Leaves the entire `.abcd/` namespace intact" — no mention of any provenance record.
discrepancies.reality: `abcd ahoy uninstall --help`: "Remove the marker block, abcd's owned PATH copy, and its provenance record (leaves .abcd/ intact)". The provenance record is `~/.abcd/path-entry` (internal/core/ahoy/owned_copy.go:43-58) — a user-scope file uninstall deletes, which this chapter never names. commands/ahoy.md also documents "along with its provenance record" and "The persistent download cache is left to the harness's own uninstall to delete"; neither appears here.

discrepancies.claim: The `~/.abcd/` layout block enumerates the user-scope directory as `history/`, `config.json` (a later phase) and `memory/` (a later phase) — presented as the complete "one user-scope directory for machine-local state".
discrepancies.reality: The live tree holds `history/`, `sources/` and `voyage/` (plus `path-entry` once an owned copy is installed). `~/.abcd/voyage/` is written by the shipped `disembark` verb (internal/core/lifeboat/voyage.go:59-66: `abcdDir := filepath.Join(home, ".abcd")`, `base := filepath.Join(abcdDir, "voyage")`), and `~/.abcd/sources/` is the corpus the shipped `/abcd:ingest` and `/abcd:consult` commands read and write (commands/ingest.md:9, commands/consult.md:8). None of the three is marked staged or later-phase in this diagram; they are simply absent.

discrepancies.claim: "The history store … its `index.json` is the **sole user-scope registry** (identity and lineage keyed on each repo's immutable root-commit SHA)." Repeated at line 352-354: "The history `index.json` is the **sole user-scope registry** — there is no `workspaces.json`."
discrepancies.reality: Two other user-scope stores keyed on abcd state ship today: `~/.abcd/voyage/<root-sha>/disembark/history.jsonl` (internal/core/lifeboat/voyage.go:45-75), keyed on the repo's root-commit SHA exactly as index.json is, and `~/.abcd/path-entry` (internal/core/ahoy/owned_copy.go:43-58), the install-ownership record. "Sole" no longer holds.

discrepancies.claim: The detection pass is enumerated as steps 0-11 (folder classification, plugin root, adapter probe, `.abcd/` skeleton, identity, history-store wiring, visibility, marker drift, PATH entry, hook manifest, version, name-banlist). The gap-category table lists `plugin-owned` examples as the marker block and hooks.json verification, and `config-change` as visibility, oracle adapter, PATH symlink, git-identity pin.
discrepancies.reality: The shipped detection pass also runs a guard-health probe and a citations probe that the step list never mentions. internal/core/ahoy/detect.go:82-87 computes `detectGuardHealth` "for every managed or adoptable repo" and appends `detectGuardGaps(...)`; internal/core/ahoy/guard_health.go emits `guard.hook_missing` and `guard.binary_unreachable` (category plugin-owned) and `guard.registry_unloadable` (category config-change) — `guard.binary_unreachable` is live in this repo's `abcd ahoy dry-run` output. detect.go:56-57 sets the `citations` signal. Both feed documented outputs (the `guard` envelope key at line 429-431, the citations line at 48-49) that no detection step produces in the record.

discrepancies.claim: "Every event command is a self-provisioning shim … the non-SessionStart shims attempt `hooks/bootstrap.sh` when the plugin-root binary is missing (throttled by a `.bootstrap.attempt` marker within a 10-minute window), then fall back to a PATH-resolved `abcd` before failing loudly."
discrepancies.reality: The shipped `SessionEnd` command in hooks/hooks.json makes no bootstrap attempt and writes no `.bootstrap.attempt` marker: it is `[ -f "$r/abcd" ] && [ -x "$r/abcd" ] && exec "$r/abcd" hook session-end; command -v abcd … && exec abcd hook session-end;` then the failure printf. Only UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse and PreCompact carry the bootstrap-plus-throttle preamble the claim attributes to all non-SessionStart shims.

discrepancies.claim: The bare status board is enumerated three times as: folder kind, plugin-root status, root SHA, binary vintage/staleness, citations (managed repo), gap count, guard health, and the banlist block.
discrepancies.reality: The renderer also prints an install-mode line — internal/surface/cli/cli.go:1780 `if mode, _ := res.Signals["install_mode"].(string); mode != ""` — and the shipped plugin surface requires it be reported: commands/ahoy.md, "`signals.install_mode` … Report it so a dev install — or an entry abcd wrote that is not the one that runs — is never invisible." `install_mode` appears nowhere in this chapter's status-board enumerations or in the dry-run `signals` description.

discrepancies.claim: "The review reaches a model through the oracle seam, host-delegated by default (per adr-25); an opt-in oracle adapter (native / CLI / API / MCP) runs it when wired — never blocks." Stated unqualified — no staged / design-target / later-phase marker, unlike the markers this chapter uses elsewhere (lines 35, 73, 111, 117).
discrepancies.reality: The shipped `abcd disembark review <lifeboat-dir> <source-repo>` has exactly two modes and no oracle seam: a deterministic mapping (internal/core/lifeboat/synthesis_review.go:180 `deterministicVerdict` over manifest-verified + coverage summary) and validation of a host-produced JSON handed in via `--review-json <file|->`. Verified: `./bin/abcd-darwin-arm64 disembark review <lb> <src>` printed `verdict: NEEDS_WORK / mode: deterministic`. No oracle adapter exists anywhere in the binary — grep for `Oracle` across non-test Go finds a single hit, internal/core/ahoy/detect.go:342, a config prompt ("Oracle backend (host-delegated/native/cli/api/mcp)"); the resulting `oracle.backend` key is written by ahoy (internal/core/ahoy/apply.go:391) and read by no consumer, so there is nothing to "wire". The repo's own record says so outright: .abcd/development/intents/planned/itd-125-...md states "the binary verb never invokes the oracle seam" and that `disembark oracle` was "a compute-or-ingest verdict endpoint" — which is why spc-30/itd-125 renamed it to `review`. The real host-delegated path is the host running agents/lifeboat-reviewer.md per commands/disembark.md:170 and feeding the result back through `--review-json`; the chapter describes a seam and an adapter class that do not exist.

discrepancies.claim: "Bare `/abcd:disembark` prints the sub-verb list and flags only" and "Current sub-verbs (as the shipped binary exposes them)", followed by an enumeration that names no flag except `--json` (line 121). Line 34 groups all four synthesis sub-verbs as "Each is deterministic-or-validate-host-JSON".
discrepancies.reality: Four sub-verb flags ship and are recorded in the committed snapshot .abcd/development/release/surface.json, but the chapter names none of them: `disembark review --review-json <file|->`, `disembark graveyard --lessons-json <file|->`, `disembark press-release --press-release-json <file|->`, `disembark principles --principles-json <file|->`. The omission hides an asymmetry the chapter's blanket wording papers over: `--lessons-json` is REQUIRED — `./bin/abcd-darwin-arm64 disembark graveyard <lb>` exits 2 with "abcd: disembark graveyard: --lessons-json <file|-> is required", i.e. `graveyard` has no deterministic mode at all, while `review`, `press-release` and `principles` all ran deterministically with no flag.

discrepancies.claim: § 5 Output shape gives the full lifeboat tree, then line 100: "The synthesis sub-verbs add the rest over an already-packed lifeboat: `press-release` writes `press-release.{json,md}`, `principles` writes `principles.{json,md}`, `review` writes the verdict artefact, and `graveyard` validates and writes the lesson JSON." — the last two named without paths, and the tree shows `graveyard/` holding only `abandoned.json` and `archaeology.json`.
discrepancies.reality: `review` creates a whole directory the § 5 tree never mentions: running it on a packed lifeboat produced `review/review-5f191252552d.json` and `review/review-5f191252552d.md` (path echoed by the binary as `review: review/review-5f191252552d.json`). `graveyard` writes `graveyard/lessons.json` plus a `graveyard/low-confidence/` directory (internal/core/lifeboat/graveyard_lessons.go:161, :232, :240) — both inside the `graveyard/` the tree shows as a two-file section. By contrast the two documented ones were exact: `press-release.{json,md}` and `principles.{json,md}` landed at the lifeboat root as stated. A reader of § 5 has no way to know a top-level `review/` directory and two further `graveyard/` entries appear.

discrepancies.claim: The shipped `probe` sub-verb bullet states it will "show what would land where, run schema/audit checks, write nothing" — an unmarked present-tense claim that probe runs an audit check.
discrepancies.reality: `EmbarkProbe` (internal/core/lifeboat/embark.go:43) runs exactly two gates: manifest verification against the on-disk tree, and a schema-version gate (`lifeboat schema v%d; this abcd knows up to v%d`). Grepping `audit` across internal/core/lifeboat/embark.go returns no hit at all — nothing in the embark path runs any audit. `audit/**` in a lifeboat is only counted as a report-only ignored file. The one audit hook the chapter describes, `--refresh-audit`, is itself marked "design target, not yet shipped", so no shipped code path can satisfy this claim.

discrepancies.claim: The probe acceptance criterion says the run inspects "(file tree, schema validation, would-be writes)" and "the user sees a report ready to inform the decision" — and the probe sub-verb bullet (line 44) describes the same output. Neither mentions the coverage handoff, conflicts, the ignored tally, or the record manifest hash.
discrepancies.reality: The shipped `embark probe` renders the coverage blanks FIRST and most prominently — `coverage blanks — answer these first (15 of 23 sections)` with a per-section question and a `(human-owned — yours to write)` marker — then the plan, then a bulk `conflicts` block, then `ignored (not embarked): N report-only, N unmapped, N unknown`, then `record manifest sha256:`. `EmbarkPlan.Render()` (internal/core/lifeboat/embark_render.go:19) and the JSON `coverage`/`conflicts`/`ignored`/`record_manifest_sha256` fields confirm this, and commands/embark.md instructs the agent to "Surface the coverage blanks to the human before anything else — they are the point of the handoff." The brief's own probe surface spec omits the shipped probe's headline output entirely (it appears only in §3 step 4, for `from`).

discrepancies.claim: §3 step 4 lists what `from` reports: "the `written`/`unchanged` counts, the per-family counts, the marker action, the coverage blanks a human must answer, and the report-only files that informed the run but were not written."
discrepancies.reality: `EmbarkResult.Render()` (internal/core/lifeboat/embark_render.go:43) emits only the coverage blanks, `embarked <src> into <tgt>`, `written: N (adrs 1, issues 1, …)`, `unchanged: N`, and `marker: CLAUDE.md installed` — it never calls `renderIgnoredSummary`, which is reached only from `EmbarkPlan.Render()` (probe). Confirmed on a live run: `embark from` printed no `ignored (not embarked)` line. The report-only file list reaches the surface only in the `--json` payload's `ignored` array; the human-facing `from` report the chapter describes does not carry it.

discrepancies.claim: The plain-text `--dry-run` render "prints only version, files bundled, scan hardfails, citations, and would-publish, plus a would-refuse-on line when there is a finding" — an exhaustive five-line enumeration that omits any receipts line from the text render (the semantic-receipts row is described only as a JSON `{"status": "host-run"}` row).
discrepancies.reality: `abcd launch --dry-run` prints six lines: version, `files bundled`, `scan hardfails`, `citations`, `receipts`, `would publish`. The receipts line is emitted by the text renderer at internal/surface/cli/cli.go:298 (`fmt.Fprintf(w, "  receipts:       %s\n", ...)`), sitting between citations and would-publish. Observed output: `receipts:       no receipts recorded for 6e4d537; the release branch is two commits — the CHANGELOG roll, then the receipts naming it (see .abcd/development/release-gate/README.md)`.

discrepancies.claim: Acceptance bullet for bare `/abcd:launch` names "the available sub-verbs (`ship`, `dry-run`)" — a two-item enumeration of what ships.
discrepancies.reality: Three sub-verb forms ship: `abcd launch --dry-run`, `abcd launch ship`, and `abcd launch scaffold`. `scaffold` is shipped per the chapter's own Sub-verbs table (line 14) and its own bullet (line 21), and appears in `abcd launch --help` and in the committed command-tree snapshot .abcd/development/release/surface.json (`abcd launch scaffold`). The bullet's "Design target" marker covers the status render, not the stale sub-verb enumeration inside it.

discrepancies.claim: The `ship` bullet describes the shipped `abcd launch ship` as deriving the version and record set, running the surface guardrail, validating with `--changelog-json` and writing the CHANGELOG heading — with no mention that the verb has a refusal path or a non-zero exit. Exit codes are documented for bare `abcd launch` (exit 1, line 18) and for `scaffold` (0/1/2, line 21), but never for `ship`.
discrepancies.reality: `abcd launch ship` has a first-class refusal surface that exits 1. Run in this tree it prints `abcd launch ship — REFUSED (base v0.6.1)` with `refused (release-in-flight): release v0.6.2 in flight — tag pending (the newest CHANGELOG heading is ahead of v0.6.1)` and `guard: (not run)`; exit code 1. The refusal kinds are a typed enum in internal/core/release/emit.go (`RefusalKind`, incl. `RefusalReleaseInFlight`), and the shipped help string itself says "exit 1 when the cut refuses". The guardrail is skipped entirely on a refusal, which the chapter's unconditional "runs the surface guardrail" does not admit.

discrepancies.claim: Acceptance criterion (unmarked, about the shipped dry-run): "when `/abcd:launch dry-run` runs, then the report lists exactly the include/exclude artefact manifest in § 2" — i.e. the preview renders both sides of the § 2 include/exclude manifest.
discrepancies.reality: The dry-run report renders the include side only. `ResolveBundle` (internal/core/launch/bundle.go:103) walks the include roots from `.abcd/config/launch-payload.json`, so a denied namespace such as `.abcd/**` never becomes a walk candidate and can never appear in `Bundle.Excluded`. `abcd launch --dry-run --json` returns `"excluded": null` (also `rejected: null`, `warnings: null`) against a clean tree, and the plain-text render prints only `files bundled:  105` — no per-file list on either side.

discrepancies.claim: "**Bare-command-as-help is a universal abcd convention** — every command in the surface set (the enumeration lives in the surfaces README) shows status + suggested next actions when invoked without args." Stated as universal, present tense, no marker.
discrepancies.reality: Not universal, and the next-actions half ships nowhere. Bare `abcd guard`, `abcd docs`, `abcd disembark`, `abcd embark` and `abcd intent audit` print cobra help with no status board; bare `abcd update` is not read-only at all — it attempts the update and exited 1 with `abcd: update refused (foreign)`. The very README this line cites says the opposite at 04-surfaces/README.md:34: "Bare-command-as-status is a common abcd convention, not a universal one" and "The suggested-next-actions half of this convention is a design target: no shipped bare invocation yet emits next actions".

discrepancies.claim: The canonical create row: "A leading quote always creates — never falls through to bare render".
discrepancies.reality: A quoted single word never creates. `./bin/abcd-darwin-arm64 intent "shape"` → exit 2, `abcd: unknown intent subcommand "shape" (nothing created — a lone word is read as a sub-verb, never as a draft title…)`; `intent "reddy"` → exit 2 with a did-you-mean-"ready" correction; `intent "audit"` dispatches to the audit sub-verb and prints its help. commands/intent.md:69-71 documents this refusal; the brief page does not, and its "always creates" is contradicted by the binary.

discrepancies.claim: §2 row for `/abcd:intent audit <itd-N>`: "Compares the intent's press release + acceptance criteria against delivered reality (code, configs, docs, tests). Per-criterion verdicts … appended to the intent's `## Audit Notes`." Same framing at line 13 ("once intent-auditor's Role 1 has run on it via `/abcd:intent audit <itd-N>`") and line 351.
discrepancies.reality: The shipped verb performs no comparison and writes no verdict. `internal/surface/cli/cli.go:1611-1636` — "bare `audit <itd-N>` re-emits the OWED stub + ephemeral request for a shipped intent" — calls `intent.ReEmitAudit`, which per `internal/core/intent/audit.go:26-33` "parks an OWED stub in the shipped intent's Audit Notes and writes an ephemeral review request under .abcd/.work.local/reviews/". A per-criterion verdict reaches `## Audit Notes` only via `audit ingest --verdict-json`. The binary's own Short string is "re-emit a shipped intent's request, or ingest a verdict".

discrepancies.claim: "**`shipped/`** — a capability built in Go. Empty until the Go build ships capabilities into it (Phase 1 onward)."
discrepancies.reality: `shipped/` is not empty. `./bin/abcd-darwin-arm64 intent` renders "drafts 67 · planned 43 · shipped 18 · disciplines 7 · superseded 4" — 18 intents already sit in .abcd/development/intents/shipped/ (itd-3, itd-46, itd-80, itd-94, …).

discrepancies.claim: In the press-release template: "# The eight keys below are the canonical seed skeleton the quoted-text create writes:".
discrepancies.reality: Six keys follow the comment (spec_id, kind, suggested_kind, reclassification_history, builds_on, severity). The shipped seed writes eight — `internal/core/intent/create.go:226-235` emits id, slug, spec_id, kind, suggested_kind, reclassification_history, builds_on, severity — but id and slug sit ABOVE the comment in the template, so the count and the word "below" cannot both be right.

discrepancies.claim: The template's "Added later, not part of the seed skeleton" list enumerates exactly three post-seed keys — `bundle`, `impact`, `surface_history` — and §1's seed list (line 132-136) enumerates six seed keys.
discrepancies.reality: `promoted_from` is missing from both lists. `internal/core/intent/create.go:238-241` writes `promoted_from: <iss-N>` into the seed "when the draft graduated from an issue", and `internal/core/intent/lifecycle.go:79` parses it back as a first-class field. Two records in the tree carry it: intents/planned/itd-131-managed-repo-identity-gate.md and intents/planned/itd-132-hook-binary-to-persistent-data-dir.md.

discrepancies.claim: "lint verifies that *all* members of a bundle reference the same bundle ID, and that bundles are bidirectional in their members' frontmatter. **Exception for superseded bundle-members:** … carry `bundle: null` AND `bundle_at_supersession: <bundle-id>` … Lint enforces this exception." Present tense, no later-phase marker (unlike IL011 at line 62).
discrepancies.reality: No shipped lint reads either field. `grep -rn "bundle_at_supersession" internal/` returns nothing; `validateIntent` (internal/core/lint/lint.go:1872-1941), the whole of `intent_lifecycle`, checks only `status`, `kind`, `spec_id` and `superseded_by`, and the string "bundle" appears there only as the kind value `bundle-member`. The page contradicts itself at line 62: "the shipped record lint has no bundle check".

discrepancies.claim: "**Every intent in `superseded/` has both `superseded_by: <handle>` AND `kind_at_supersession: <original-kind>`.** … Both are required." Listed as a thing §6's lint "verifies".
discrepancies.reality: `kind_at_supersession` is enforced by nothing. It appears in no Go file (`grep -rn "kind_at_supersession" internal/` is empty); internal/core/lint/lint.go:1917-1932 requires only `superseded_by` matching `^(itd|adr)-\d+` plus a non-null `kind`. `record_schema` (internal/core/lint/schema.go) validates ids/slugs and cross-store link targets, not this field.

discrepancies.claim: "The shipped record-lint subset is the `intent_lifecycle` rule (the directory/kind/`spec_id` invariants and the `status:`-key ban below), the `intent_impact_valid` rule …, and `persona_registry`" — presented as the complete shipped set over the intent tree.
discrepancies.reality: `record_schema` is also armed over the itd store and is load-bearing for intents: .abcd/record-lint.json configures `record_schema.record_stores.itd = .abcd/development/intents`, and internal/core/lint/lint.go:101-105 states that a repo running `intent_lifecycle` alone accepts `superseded_by: adr-9999` and that "record_schema is what closes that — it reads every store and resolves cross-store targets — so the two rules are armed together". `intent_lifecycle` also runs an id-uniqueness leg (validateIntentIDUnique, lint.go:1677) that the parenthetical scope does not name.

discrepancies.claim: "`suggested_kind: decision` validates in the schema but is REFUSED by `plan_single`/`reclassify` (\"decisions are not plannable\")." Present-tense, inside a paragraph whose later-phase marker covers the itd-44 capture verdict, not this validation claim.
discrepancies.reality: Neither half exists. No shipped schema validates `suggested_kind` at all — `grep -rn suggested_kind internal/core/lint/ internal/core/intent/` (non-test) hits only create.go:232, which writes the literal `null`. `plan_single` is a symbol from the predecessor tooling: `grep -rn "plan_single\|planSingle" internal/ cmd/` returns nothing; the shipped entry point is `intent.Plan` (internal/core/intent/lifecycle.go:98), and no `reclassify` sub-verb is registered (`abcd intent --help` lists audit, link, new, plan, ready).

discrepancies.claim: Frontmatter schema block annotates the id field `id: iss-N  # unpadded, mirrors itd-N` — i.e. a small unpadded sequential integer allocated the same way an itd-N is.
discrepancies.reality: The shipped allocator mints a native 16-digit timestamp id: `internal/core/capture/alloc.go` reservePath routes through `recordid.Minter` and its comment states "The mint consults no maximum — not the ledger's, not the refs' (adr-45 ruling 2)"; `internal/core/recordid/mint_test.go` pins the shape `^iss-[0-9]{16}$` (`iss-2608201142070789` = family tag + 12-digit UTC yymmddHHMMSS + 4-digit entropy). Live ledger confirms: `abcd capture` renders `iss-2608231409595789`, and the on-disk record carries `id: "iss-2608231409595789"`. itd-N is NOT minted the same way — `internal/core/intent/create.go` nextIntentID is still a max+1 scan (`return fmt.Sprintf("itd-%d", max+1)`), so the two families no longer mirror each other at all.

discrepancies.claim: §4 acceptance example: "an existing issue at `.abcd/work/issues/open/iss-3-foo.md` … the file moves to `.abcd/work/issues/resolved/iss-3-foo.md`" — small-integer ids presented as the current filename layout.
discrepancies.reality: No new issue can be filed under that shape; every id minted since adr-45/spc-33 is 16 digits (`iss-2608231025198888-abcd-capture-writes-to-the-ledger.md`). Small-integer names survive only as legacy records already on disk (iss-33, iss-202). The acceptance criterion describes a filename the shipped mint cannot produce.

discrepancies.claim: §2 "Ledger structure" documents the ledger as the three status folders plus `iss-N-<slug>.md` files and the frontmatter schema — nothing else.
discrepancies.reality: The shipped ledger root also holds two artefacts the chapter never names, both COMMITTED (`git ls-files .abcd/work/issues/` returns them): `.iss-alloc.lock`, the allocator flock created by `ensureLedgerDirs`/`withLedgerLock` (internal/core/capture/alloc.go, `const lockFilename = ".iss-alloc.lock"`), and `README.md`. A reader provisioning or auditing the ledger from this chapter would not expect either.

discrepancies.claim: §1 enumerates the capture write paths (text capture, resolve, wontfix) with no mention of any transformation of the caller's text — the chapter never uses the word redact and describes the write as "appends a structured issue entry to the ledger".
discrepancies.reality: Every ledger write path redacts the free text before writing and reports a count. `internal/core/capture/redact.go` runs `redactLedgerText`/`redactCaptureInputs` through the shared `internal/adapter/scanner`, rewriting the capture text, the derived slug, the resolution note and the wontfix reason; `redact_test.go` pins TestCaptureRedactsHomePathOnWrite, TestCaptureWithHomePathInDerivedSlugStillFiles and TestResolveRedactsTheNote. A degraded scanner still redacts and returns a reason. The shipped plugin surface documents this (`commands/capture.md`: "Report `redacted` too whenever it is non-zero: it counts the spans rewritten before the text was written, and the user needs to know their wording was changed"). The brief chapter is silent, so the record does not say the user's wording can be changed on write.

discrepancies.claim: The only refusal the chapter documents on the capture surface is the unfiltered `abcd capture list`, "rejected with exit 2 and a 'choose a filter: --open / --resolved / --wontfix / --all' message".
discrepancies.reality: The shipped verb carries a second, separately-reasoned exit-2 refusal on the text-capture path that the chapter never mentions: a whitespace-free single word is read as a mistyped sub-verb and nothing is written — `abcd capture typo` → exit 2, "unknown capture subcommand \"typo\" (nothing captured — a lone word is read as a sub-verb, never as issue text; issue text must contain a space, so write the whole sentence)" — and a near-miss of a real sub-verb is refused with the correction named — `abcd capture reslove iss-1 "x"` → exit 2, "unknown capture subcommand \"reslove\"; did you mean \"resolve\"?". `commands/capture.md` documents both; the brief does not, so §1's "fast path" row implies any quoted text files an issue.

discrepancies.claim: The chapter documents the capture surface end-to-end (sub-verbs, flags, ledger schema, acceptance) without ever mentioning a machine-readable render.
